dedupe_keys.name: interactive map of planned solar power plants in hungary from 2016 kat permits energiaklub

description: Energiaklub, a Hungarian energy policy think tank, published in May 2018 an interactive map showing where investors planned to build solar power plants in Hungary. It was built from the permits issued during the 2016 rush for the feed-in tariff scheme (KÁT), under which the energy regulator MEKH licensed renewable plants to sell electricity above the market price for a set period; roughly 2,000 permits were issued for plants of 500 kW or less. Because the regulator did not release a summary table, Energiaklub processed the scanned permits one by one: 1,917 permits with a total capacity of 930 MW. The map, made with ArcGIS, shows red circles next to settlements that open the permitted capacity, and the page notes that the data matters for the system operator and for grid development planning because of where capacity will connect. Access is free online; the site states all rights reserved. Caveats stated on the page: later changes to site permits are not included, only permits the regulator published are covered, and 2017 and 2018 permits are left out, though they were few. Coverage is Hungary at settlement level. It supports capacity planning for distribution grids and hazard exposure studies of distributed solar generation; the related record is the Roofpedia green and solar roofs dataset.
